questions.q: Match the type of uveitis with its alternative name — 1) Anterior uveitis  2) Intermediate uveitis  3) Posterior uveitis  … A) Chorioretinitis/Retinochoroiditis  B) Pars planitis/Posterior cyclitis  C) Iridocyclitis
questions.exp: AKA row: anterior uveitis - iridocyclitis; intermediate uveitis - pars planitis/posterior cyclitis; posterior uveitis - chorioretinitis/retinochoroiditis. (Book p185)

questions.q: Which type of uveitis has a dash (no alternative name) in the AKA row of the table?
questions.exp: AKA row: pan uveitis shows '-'. (Book p185)

questions.q: In anterior uveitis, involvement of the iris is called iritis, and involvement of the pars plicata is called ___.
questions.exp: Involvement of AU: Iris: Iritis; Pars plicata: Cyclitis. (Book p185)

questions.q: In intermediate uveitis, inflammation of the vitreous is termed:
questions.exp: Intermediate uveitis: peripheral retina - basal retinochoroiditis; vitreous - vitritis/hyalitis. (Book p185)

questions.q: Match the type of uveitis with the tissue involved — 1) Posterior uveitis  2) Pan uveitis  … A) All layers of uvea  B) Iris and pars plicata  C) Choroid & retina
questions.exp: Involvement of: posterior uveitis - choroid & retina; pan uveitis - all layers of uvea. (Book p185)

questions.q: In the clinical classification, acute uveitis has a duration of:
questions.exp: Acute: duration < 3 months. (Book p185)

questions.q: A uveitis lasts more than 3 months and relapses within less than 3 months. Which clinical class is this?
questions.exp: Chronic: duration > 3 months + relapse in < 3 months. (Book p185)

questions.q: Recurrent uveitis is defined by at least how long between two episodes?
questions.exp: Recurrent: >= 3 months b/w 2 episodes. (Book p185)

questions.q: The etiological classification of uveitis divides it into:
questions.exp: Etiological classification: granulomatous; non-granulomatous. (Book p185)

questions.q: In anterior uveitis, pain is referred along the branches of the ___ nerve.
questions.exp: SYMPTOMS: Pain: referred along branches of 5th nerve. (Book p185)

questions.q: Redness is a symptom of anterior uveitis. The blurring of vision is due to which two causes?
questions.exp: Symptoms: redness; blurring of vision d/t corneal haze and aqueous turbidity. (Book p185)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the listed symptoms of anterior uveitis?
opts: Sudden painless loss of vision with a clear cornea
Pain referred along branches of the 5th nerve
questions.exp: Symptoms: pain, redness, blurring of vision, severe photophobia, lacrimation. (Book p185)

questions.q: The conjunctival sign of anterior uveitis is ___.
questions.exp: SIGNS 1. Conjunctiva: Circumcorneal congestion. (Book p186)

questions.q: Corneal haze in anterior uveitis is due to:
questions.exp: 2. Cornea: Corneal haze d/t raised intraocular pressure (IOP)/toxins. (Book p186)

questions.q: Keratic precipitates are cellular deposits on the corneal ___, most commonly in ___ triangle.
questions.exp: KPs: cellular deposits on corneal endothelium; location: Arlt's triangle (m/c). (Book p186)

questions.q: Match the KP type with the uveitis and content — 1) Mutton fat KPs  2) Fine granules KPs  … A) Non-granulomatous uveitis, contain lymphocytes  B) Granulomatous uveitis, contain macrophages  C) Chronic non-granulomatous uveitis
questions.exp: Mutton fat: granulomatous uveitis, contain macrophages. Fine granules: non-granulomatous uveitis, contain lymphocytes. (Book p186)

questions.q: KPs are pigmented in a patient with long-standing uveitis. Which uveitis does the book list for pigmented KPs?
questions.exp: Pigmented KPs: seen in chronic non-granulomatous uveitis. (Book p186)

questions.q: Stellate (star-shaped, diffusely distributed) KPs are seen in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Stellate KPs: herpetic uveitis, toxoplasmosis, Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis (FHI); star-shaped; diffuse distribution. (Book p186)

questions.q: Aqueous cells are markers of ___.
questions.exp: Anterior chamber: 1. Aqueous cells: markers of disease activity. (Book p186)

questions.q: Aqueous flare is turbidity of aqueous due to leakage of ___, and is visible due to the ___.
questions.exp: 2. Aqueous flare: turbidity of aqueous d/t leakage of proteins; visible d/t Tyndall effect/Brownian movement. (Book p186)

questions.q: In the slit lamp figure captioned 'Aqueous cells', the two arrows label:
questions.exp: Figure caption: Aqueous cells; labels: Aqueous, Cornea. (Book p186)

questions.q: A patient has anterior uveitis with a hypopyon. Which disease does the book link to this combination?
questions.exp: 3. Hypopyon: hypopyon + anterior uveitis: Behcet's disease. (Book p186)

questions.q: Hyphema with anterior uveitis is seen in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: 4. Hyphema + AU: herpetic uveitis, toxoplasmosis, syphilis. (Behcet's disease is the cause linked to hypopyon.) (Book p186)

questions.q: Pseudo-rubiosis of the iris is due to ___.
opts: Iris neovascularisation from posterior segment hypoxia
questions.exp: Iris: 1. Pseudo-rubiosis: d/t dilated iris vessels. (Book p186)

questions.q: Muddy iris is seen in acute cases and is also known as:
questions.exp: 2. Muddy iris: seen in acute cases; AKA water logged iris. (Book p186)

questions.q: Match the type of iris atrophy (seen in chronic cases) with its uveitis — 1) Sectoral  2) Diffuse  … A) FHI  B) Herpetic uveitis  C) Behcet's disease
questions.exp: 3. Iris atrophy: seen in chronic cases. Types: sectoral - herpetic uveitis; diffuse - FHI. (Book p186)

questions.q: Match the iris nodule with its location — 1) Koeppe nodules  2) Busacca nodules  … A) Iris stroma  B) Pupillary margin  C) Angle of anterior chamber
questions.exp: Location: Koeppe nodules - pupillary margin; Busacca nodules - iris stroma. (Book p187)

questions.q: Iris nodules are seen in granulomatous as well as non granulomatous uveitis. Which nodules are these, when Busacca nodules are seen only in granulomatous uveitis?
questions.exp: Found in: Koeppe nodules - granulomatous and non granulomatous uveitis; Busacca nodules - granulomatous uveitis. (Book p187)

questions.q: The two iris photographs with red arrows are captioned:
opts: Koeppe nodules and Sectoral iris atrophy
questions.exp: Captions: Koeppe nodules; Busacca nodules. (Book p187)

questions.q: Miosis is seen in ___ cases of anterior uveitis.
questions.exp: Pupil: 1. Miosis: Acute cases. (Book p187)

questions.q: A chronic anterior uveitis shows a festooned pupil. What is the mechanism given in the book?
opts: 360° posterior synechiae stop aqueous flow to the anterior chamber
Exudates organise across the anterior surface of the pupil
Exudation forms incomplete posterior synechiae; the pupil dilates irregularly
Loss of iris crypts causes irregular dilation
questions.exp: 2. Festooned pupil: chronic cases. Exudation -> incomplete posterior synechiae (adhesion b/w pupillary margin and lens) -> dilates the pupil -> irregular dilation. (Book p187)

questions.q: Recurrent anterior uveitis leaves a fixed pupil due to annular (ring/complete) posterior synechiae with 360° adhesion. What follows?
opts: Decreased IOP from no aqueous secretion
No aqueous flow from posterior to anterior chamber, causing secondary angle closure glaucoma
questions.exp: 3. Fixed pupil: recurrent cases; annular/ring/complete posterior synechiae (360° adhesion) -> no aqueous flow from posterior chamber to anterior chamber -> secondary angle closure glaucoma. (Book p187)

questions.q: Total posterior synechiae is adhesion between the ___ surface of the iris and the lens.
questions.exp: 4. Total Posterior Synechiae (TPS): exudation in posterior chamber -> adhesion b/w posterior surface of iris and lens. (Book p187)

questions.q: TPS together with exudates leaking behind the lens covers the ciliary processes, equator and posterior surface of the lens. What is this, and what happens to IOP?
opts: Cyclitic membrane; IOP increases as aqueous cannot drain
Cyclitic membrane; IOP decreases as no aqueous is secreted
questions.exp: 5. Cyclitic membrane: TPS + exudates leak behind lens; covers ciliary processes, equator & posterior surface of lens -> no aqueous secretion -> decreased IOP. (Book p187)

questions.q: Exudates organised across the anterior surface of the pupil constitute:
questions.exp: 6. Occlusio pupillae: exudates organised across anterior surface of pupil. (Book p187)

questions.q: In acute anterior uveitis, IOP is raised. What are the reasons given?
opts: Cyclitic membrane and shut down of the ciliary body
Annular posterior synechiae with no aqueous flow
Trabecular meshwork blockage by cells and proteins, plus associated trabeculitis
Total posterior synechiae behind the lens
questions.exp: IOP - Acute AU: raised IOP d/t trabecular meshwork blockage by cells and proteins + associated trabeculitis. (Book p188)

questions.q: True or false — 'Chronic anterior uveitis causes raised IOP because of trabeculitis.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: True - chronic AU raises IOP by trabecular blockage
False - chronic AU gives decreased IOP due to trabecular meshwork blockage
False - chronic AU gives decreased IOP due to cyclitic membrane and shut down of ciliary body
True - chronic AU raises IOP due to cyclitic membrane
questions.exp: IOP - Chronic AU: decreased IOP d/t cyclitic membrane + shut down of ciliary body. (Acute AU: raised IOP.) (Book p188)

questions.q: The most common cataract complication of uveitis, complicated cataract, has a bread crumb appearance plus ___.
questions.exp: 1. Complicated Cataract: m/c; bread crumb appearance + polychromatic lustre. (Book p188)

questions.q: Per the mnemonic UMAR for causes of complicated cataract, which of the following is NOT a listed cause?
questions.exp: Mnemonic UMAR: Uveitis, Myopia, Angle closure glaucoma, Retinitis pigmentosa. (Book p188)

questions.q: In the mnemonic UMAR, the letter A stands for:
questions.exp: UMAR: Uveitis, Myopia, Angle closure glaucoma, Retinitis pigmentosa. (Book p188)

questions.q: Which complication of anterior uveitis is most common in recurrent cases?
questions.exp: 2. Secondary angle closure glaucoma: m/c in recurrent cases. (Book p188)

questions.q: Band shaped keratopathy in anterior uveitis is caused by calcium deposits in which layer?
questions.exp: 3. Band shaped keratopathy: calcium deposits in Bowman's layer of cornea. (Book p188)

questions.q: Which complication is the most common cause of visual loss due to posterior involvement in anterior uveitis?
questions.exp: 4. Cystoid macular edema: m/c cause of visual loss d/t posterior involvement in anterior uveitis (AU). (Book p188)

questions.q: Under the treatment of anterior uveitis, which drug is listed as the antimetabolite (topical steroids listed are prednisolone and difluprednate)?
questions.exp: Topical steroids: prednisolone, difluprednate. Antimetabolites: azathioprine. Cycloplegics: atropine. (Book p188)

questions.q: When is azathioprine given in anterior uveitis?
opts: When there is a cyclitic membrane with decreased IOP
When there is inflammation with recurrent episodes requiring long term steroids
For pain relief by relaxing the ciliary muscle
When posterior synechiae must be broken
questions.exp: Antimetabolites: Azathioprine - given if inflammation + recurrent episodes requiring long term steroids. (Book p188)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as an action of atropine in anterior uveitis?
opts: Relaxing the ciliary muscle for pain relief
questions.exp: Cycloplegics: atropine - relax ciliary muscle -> pain relief; break posterior synechiae; prevent formation of posterior synechiae. (Book p188)

questions.q: Match the route of steroid administration with its side effect — 1) Topical  2) Systemic  … A) Cataract  B) Glaucoma  C) Band shaped keratopathy
questions.exp: Side effects of steroids: topical administration - glaucoma; systemic administration - cataract. (Book p188)

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a granulomatous cause of anterior uveitis?
questions.exp: GRANULOMATOUS: a. Tuberculosis, b. Leprosy, c. Sarcoidosis, d. Syphilis, e. Herpes. Behcet's, ankylosing spondylitis and psoriatic arthritis are under non granulomatous. (Book p189)

questions.q: In leprosy, which type is the most common cause of anterior uveitis, and which feature is pathognomonic?
questions.exp: b. Leprosy: m/c: lepromatous leprosy; iris pearls: pathognomonic feature. (Book p189)

questions.q: What is the most common ocular manifestation of sarcoidosis?
questions.exp: c. Sarcoidosis: m/c ocular manifestation of sarcoidosis: granulomatous anterior uveitis. (Book p189)

questions.q: A patient with sarcoidosis has erythema nodosum, bilateral lymphadenopathy and anterior uveitis. What is this syndrome?
questions.exp: Lofgren syndrome: Erythema nodosum + B/L lymphadenopathy + Anterior uveitis. (Book p189)

questions.q: Heerfordt syndrome is also called ___.
questions.exp: Heerfordt syndrome/uveoparotid fever. (Book p189)

questions.q: In syphilis, the m/c form of uveitis is in late congenital syphilis. What presentation is listed?
questions.exp: d. Syphilis: m/c in late congenital syphilis; presentation: iris roseolas. (Book p189)

questions.q: Anterior uveitis with raised IOP, hyphema, stellate KPs and sectoral iris atrophy points to which cause?
questions.exp: e. Herpes: AU + Raised IOP + Hyphema + Stellate KPs + Sectoral iris atrophy. (Book p189)

questions.q: Which category is the most common cause of acute non granulomatous anterior uveitis?
questions.exp: 2. NON GRANULOMATOUS - Acute: 1. Idiopathic: m/c. (Book p189)

questions.q: A patient has lower back pain with stiffness and recurrent unilateral anterior uveitis. Which HLA B27 associated disease is this?
questions.exp: 2. HLA B27 associated disease: Ankylosing spondylitis: lower back pain + stiffness + recurrent U/L AU. (Book p189)

questions.q: The triad of Reiter's disease consists of:
opts: Urethritis, arthritis and aphthous mouth ulcers
questions.exp: Reiter's disease: Triad - Conjunctivitis, Urethritis, Arthritis. (Book p189)

questions.q: Match the Reiter's disease extra-ocular feature — 1) Keratoderma blenorrhagicum  2) Circinate balanitis  … A) Skin lesions  B) Genital lesion  C) Sausage digits
questions.exp: Reiter's: + U/L AU + keratoderma blenorrhagicum + circinate balanitis + history of travel. (Book p189)

questions.q: A patient has bilateral anterior uveitis with sausage digits. Which disease is this?
questions.exp: Psoriatic arthritis: Sausage digits + B/L AU. (Book p189)

questions.q: Behcet's disease is associated with HLA ___ and B51.
questions.exp: 3. Behcet's disease: A/w HLA B5, B51. (Book p189)

questions.q: B/L recurrent anterior uveitis with a cold mobile hypopyon: which oral finding completes the book's description?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease: B/L recurrent AU + Cold mobile hypopyon + Aphthous mouth ulcers. (Book p189)

questions.q: In inflammatory bowel disease, the book gives which figures for uveitis?
questions.exp: 4. Inflammatory bowel disease: Ulcerative colitis (12%) > Crohn's disease (2.4%). (Book p189)

questions.q: The list of acute non granulomatous causes of anterior uveitis ends on this page with item 5, which is:
questions.exp: 5. Drug induced uveitis: (list continues on the next page). (Book p189)

questions.q: Drug induced uveitis mnemonic 'CML Please Relapse Slowly' — match the letter with the drug: 1) C  2) M  3) L  … A) Latanoprost  B) Cidofovir  C) Metipranolol  D) Pilocarpine
questions.exp: Mnemonic: CML Please Relapse Slowly - Cidofovir, metipranolol, Latanoprost, Pilocarpine, Rifabutin, Sulfonamides. (Book p190)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a drug in the mnemonic for drug induced uveitis?
questions.exp: The mnemonic drugs: cidofovir, metipranolol, latanoprost, pilocarpine, rifabutin, sulfonamides. Prednisolone is a topical steroid used for treatment (p188). (Book p190)

questions.q: Which condition is the most common cause of anterior uveitis in the paediatric age group?
questions.exp: Chronic: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA): m/c cause of AU in paediatric age group. (Book p190)

questions.q: Match the JIA type with the number of joints — 1) Pauciarticular  2) Polyarticular  … A) More than 4 joints  B) 4 or fewer joints  C) Systemic disease only
questions.exp: Pauciarticular: <= 4 joints involved; polyarticular: > 4 joints involved. (Book p190)

questions.q: Besides pauciarticular and polyarticular, which third type of JIA is listed?
questions.exp: JIA types: pauciarticular, polyarticular, Stills disease. (Book p190)

questions.q: A girl has pauciarticular JIA that is the m/c type in females and most commonly associated with AU. Which subtype is this?
questions.exp: Pauciarticular type 1: m/c in females; m/c a/w AU. (Book p190)

questions.q: Pauciarticular type 1 JIA is characterised by which serology?
questions.exp: Type 1: RF -ve (Seronegative); ANA +ve. (Book p190)

questions.q: Pauciarticular type 2 JIA is m/c in ___.
questions.exp: Type 2: m/c in males. (Book p190)

questions.q: In Fuch's heterochromic iridocyclitis (mnemonic NO FUCHS), which feature is absent?
questions.exp: NO FUCHS: No posterior synechiae, Floaters, Unilateral, Cataract, Heterochromia iridis, Stellate KPs. (Book p190)

questions.q: In the mnemonic NO FUCHS, the letters F, U and C stand for:
questions.exp: NO FUCHS: Floaters; Unilateral; Cataract. (Book p190)

questions.q: In FHC, the affected eye shows heterochromia iridis. What is the change and its cause?
opts: Hypochromia due to loss of iris crypts
Hyperchromia due to iris pigment deposition
Hypochromia due to dilated iris vessels
Hyperchromia due to loss of iris crypts
questions.exp: Heterochromia iridis: Hypochromia in the affected eye d/t loss of iris crypts. (Book p190)

questions.q: Which type of keratic precipitates does the NO FUCHS mnemonic end with?
questions.exp: NO FUCHS: ... Stellate keratic precipitates (S). (Book p190)

questions.q: Which sign is defined as bleeding on paracentesis in Fuch's heterochromic iridocyclitis?
questions.exp: Amsler's Sign: Bleeding on paracentesis. (Book p190)
